name: Email from Ms. Harrison
extracted_text:
Lucas Adcock <lucasadcock@gmail.com>  Request for immediate action  1 message  51-50 5-0   <imissobamausa@gmail.com>   Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 10:50 AM  To: "lucasadcock@gmail.com" <lucasadcock@gmail.com>  Dear Mr. Adcock,  I am writing to provide a factual summary of the charges and to request immediate action on this case due to my terminal health status.  1. The Defective Charge (Motion to Dismiss)  The citation/affidavit states I was arrested for Obstructing a Civil Process Server under Tenn. Code Ann. § 39-16-602(c). However, the arresting officer (Trooper Garfield, THP) was conducting a criminal investigation. There was no civil process server present, and no legal writ or process was being served. Because the elements of this specific statute do not apply to a criminal investigation, the charging document is legally defective on its face. Please file a Motion to Dismiss under Tenn. R. Crim. P. 12(b)(2)(B) for failure to state an offense.  2. The Intended Charge (The "Halo Law")  I believe the officer intended to charge me under the 2025 "Halo Law" (also known as the PEACE Act), codified at Tenn. Code Ann. § 39-16-612(a) (2025 Tenn. Pub. Acts, ch. 409). This law requires a 25-foot buffer around officers after a warning.  3. Why the Intended Charge Fails  When ordered to leave, I complied and walked away down the right of way while leaving my disabled car in place. The video evidence proves I retreated and did not approach her within the 25-foot buffer. Therefore, even the law she wanted to use does not apply.  4. Civil Rights Violations & Why the Footage Matters  As I told you at the courthouse, I have already spoken with my civil rights attorney, and he wants to take this case. The footage and data from this encounter are critical to that lawsuit because of the following rights violations:  · Fourth Amendment - Excessive Force & Unlawful Seizure: The officer placed both hands on me and squeezed my arms while I was in a compliant surrender posture. I went entirely limp to avoid a false "resisting" charge, but she continued to physically manipulate my arms.  · Fourteenth Amendment - Deliberate Indifference to a Serious Medical Need: In severe heat, she left me in the back of the patrol vehicle while she finished her initial criminal investigation. Then, during the subsequent transport to the jail, I was dry heaving from heat exhaustion. She told me it was my fault for getting arrested. Upon arriving at the jail entrance, she turned the air conditioner on.  · Fourth & Fourteenth Amendments - Reckless Endangerment of a Detainee: She was excessively speeding in a 55 mph zone while looking at and manipulating a mobile computer with her right hand while driving with her left, while I was handcuffed and unable to brace myself in the back seat. (The vehicle's GPS data will confirm the exact speed).  Because of this, obtaining a dismissal (favorable termination) on this defective charge is essential to the civil case, and the body/dash camera footage and GPS data are the primary evidence needed to prove these claims.  5. Health Status & Urgency  I have been diagnosed with terminal MDS (blood cancer) and terminal CMML (leukemia). Because my time is limited, I cannot afford to let this criminal case drag out until January at minimum. I need to resolve this so I can start my civil case, for which my attorney will be filing a motion for expedited proceedings based on my terminal diagnosis. This diagnosis is the reason I am asking for the following steps to be taken immediately:
Immediate Requests:  1. Motion to Dismiss: Please file the Motion to Dismiss based on the wrong statute now.  2. Production & Preservation: Please send a formal letter to the Tennessee Highway Patrol and the District Attorney’s office immediately to request the production of all Body Cam, Dash Cam, and In-Car audio and video, as well as the GPS telemetry data from the patrol vehicle, now. Demand they preserve all of this evidence as it contains exculpatory evidence. Additionally, please issue a subpoena duces tecum under Tenn. R. Crim. P. 1(b) and Rule 17 to the Tennessee Highway Patrol (as the custodian of records) to produce all of this footage and GPS data as soon as possible.  As you saw in the video footage I texted you, these facts are clearly documented. Please review this information and respond back with me on how we can proceed.  Thank you so much.  Sincerely,  Shelly (Shelli) Harrison  660-619-8262  GS-1124992
